history.summary: A 2,271 sqft 'cheap-PSF' freehold unit billed as a 3BR at $1,114 PSF — but that headline PSF is flattered by huge size; the absolute price is $2.53M near Dakota MRT. Freehold and a 6.37% rate are appealing, but the enormous floor area and 20-txn data make this a niche, low-liquidity buy.
history.rating_rationale: The $1,114 PSF looks like a steal versus the $1,575 median, but it is an artefact of the 2,271 sqft size (likely a penthouse/dual-level) — the $2.53M quantum is what matters and it sits in a thin, niche band for a 3-bed. The 6.37% rate rests on only 20 txns. Freehold and CC8 Dakota (~740m) are real positives, but this is an oversized-unit-as-cheap-PSF trap for an investment hold.
red_flags: 2,271 sqft is far oversized for a 3BR — cheap PSF is misleading

history.summary: Freehold 2008 3-bedroom PENTHOUSE (2,271 sqft, inside the 1,819-2,303 sqft penthouse band) in Geylang. Every 'value' signal the algo fired - age_adj -34.2%, very_low_psf, -29.6% cohort - is an artifact of comparing a huge penthouse PSF against normal stacked units, NOT a real bargain.
history.rating_rationale: Asking $2.53M at $1,114 psf for a 2,271 sqft 3BR penthouse. Web-verified: typical Atrium units transact at ~$1,538-$1,594 psf (12-month avg ~$1,571), and 2,271 sqft is a confirmed penthouse size (20 such units). The $1,114 psf asking is the standard penthouse quantum/PSF discount - large penthouses always sell far below typical-unit PSF - so the -34.2% age-adj and -29.6% cohort 'discounts' (the cohort has ZERO transactions) are pure size/format artifacts, not district underpricing. On top of that: 2008 vintage (18yr-old freehold, depreciating fittings), Geylang location with its red-light-district stigma, financing/MAS LTV constraints and weaker tenant/resale demand, only ~3.2% project rental yield, and a $2.53M quantum on a hard-to-exit penthouse. The model explains <10% of forward variance and here even its value signals are corrupted - this is an Avoid for a 5-7yr hold.
